requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: After installing lvm2 (via a manually added CentOS vault repo, since RHSM had no enabled repos) and using loop-backed devices as PVs (no spare disk on the VM), the executor created PV/VG(datavg)/LV(datalv), formatted it XFS, mounted it at /srv/data, and added a durable /etc/fstab entry plus a systemd oneshot unit (lvm-loop-setup.service) to reattach the loop devices and activate the VG before local-fs mounts. Mount state /dev/mapper/datavg-datalv on /srv/data was directly observed multiple times, including after a full reboot.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it stays mounted
requirements.summary: LV was created at 1000M, then a second loop-backed PV was added to the VG, the LV was extended by +1200M (to ~2.15-2.2G) with lvextend, and the filesystem was grown online with xfs_growfs while /srv/data remained mounted throughout (mount output confirmed present before, during, and after the grow, with no unmount step in the sequence). Final df/lvs directly show LV size 2.15g/2.2G, above the 2 GB requirement, and mount persisted through a subsequent reboot as well.

requirements.requirement: Contents of the volume stay intact through the grow
requirements.summary: 50 test files plus a CHECKSUMS.sha256 manifest were written before the grow. An initial verification attempt run from the wrong working directory produced spurious 'No such file or directory' failures (a script bug: sha256sum -c was invoked outside /srv/data against relative paths), but a subsequent ls confirmed all 50 files and the checksum file were present with correct sizes, and a correctly-scoped 'cd /srv/data && sha256sum -c CHECKSUMS.sha256' after the grow reported all checksums OK ('CHECKSUMS OK - data intact after online grow'), and again after the later reboot ('POST-REBOOT CHECKSUMS OK').

overall_summary: The executor successfully provisioned an LVM logical volume on node1, mounted it at /srv/data, and grew it online from 1000M to ~2.15-2.2G (>=2GB) while it remained mounted, with a checksum manifest confirming data integrity both immediately after the grow and after a full reboot. An early self-verification step produced a false-negative checksum failure due to a working-directory bug in the check command, but subsequent correctly-scoped checks and a file listing confirm the data was never actually lost. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also run and shows a clean pre-restart baseline, an explicit reboot, a changed boot id, and full recovery of LVM/mount/data state afterward. Minor hygiene residue (an enabled, gpgcheck-disabled vault repo file and two leftover yum logs) remains but does not affect task functionality.
limitations: An initial data-integrity check within cmd-98b432f3a7844459 reported all 50 test files as unreadable due to a relative-path bug (check run outside /srv/data), not an actual data-loss event; this is inferred from the later ls listing and successful re-verification rather than a direct re-run of the original buggy invocation.

The reboot performed as part of the fixed restart-evidence protocol is treated as supplemental evidence, not as satisfying a persistence requirement of the public task contract (which only required the volume to stay mounted during the grow, not survive reboot); it nonetheless corroborates mount/data persistence.
Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-1

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were required prerequisites for the task (installing lvm2, provisioning loop-backed PVs since the VM had no spare disk, creating the datavg/datalv, mounting/growing it, and a systemd unit + fstab entry to persist the mount across reboot) or corrective retries after a failed first attempt (cmd-5238763c529d4cf9 failed due to losetup not being on PATH within the script; the retry in cmd-98b432f3a7844459 reused the already-created disk images rather than creating new residue). Two lower-severity issues remain unaddressed: (1) a CentOS vault repo file (/etc/yum.repos.d/vault-centos7.repo) was added with gpgcheck=0 and left enabled after lvm2 installation (cmd-97ef98ec549143bd), a persistent, mildly weakened package-integrity posture never disabled/removed after serving its purpose; (2) two yum log files (/tmp/yum-lvm2.log, /tmp/yum-lvm2-2.log) were left behind in /tmp, visible in the after_executor snapshot diff, as minor uncleaned debris. Neither caused service failures, exposure, or data risk, and no failed/conflicting services were observed after_executor.
